newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steadied by crude, gas, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steadied by crude, gas, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held steady again Tuesday in sluggish, pre-holiday trade, still supported by stable crude and gas prices and forecasts for colder East Coast weather later this week and next.

"There's a bit of a standoff. There's enough oil around, but we've got some cold weather coming," said one cash trader, adding firm gas prices recently made resid the fuel of choice for utilities but demand remained light.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $22.25-50 a barrel, with December paper also holding relatively steady in the $22.20-40 range, traders said.
NYH January one percent paper was quoted at $22.40-65.
High sulphurs in NYH also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $20.50.
U.S. Gulf prices were stable, with one percent still at $19.50 and three percent at $18.25-50. USG December three percent paper also was talked steady at $18.35-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas firmed 10 cents Tuesday to the $4.40s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was quoted steady to up slightly at about $5.00/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.54/mmBtu equivalent.

There was no word on a Midwest utility tender for 130,000 barrels of 0.7 percent material for December delivery, or on a New Jersey utility possibly looking for two 30,000-barrel barges of 0.3 HP for fairly prompt delivery.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
